newsitem.title: UK: Dlr rallies in Europe on US assets and EMU hopes.
newsitem.headline: Dlr rallies in Europe on US assets and EMU hopes.

text.p: The dollar rallied more than one pfennig and half a yen in Europe on the back of a another robust rise in U.S. stocks and bonds and amid more positive sign of a Franco-German accord on the details of European monetary union.

The combination of a benign U.S. producer price report for May and a further rise in consumer sentiment in June helped the Dow Jones industrial average to extend its recent gains to record levels by more than 70 points on early trade.
Comments from the Franco-German summit in France, meantime, raised hopes of an imminent agreement on the final nuances of the post-EMU stability pact and kept traders wary of marks.

"Concerns about EMU are still there but people are so nervous now about the outcome of any talks at the weekend that they are just steering clear of the mark altogether," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America in London.

At 1514 GMT, the dollar was trading at 1.7370/75 marks compared with 1.7260/65 late Friday, more than regaining the EMU-inspired losses it suffered since closing in Europe at 1.7250/60 late last week.
Traders said that speculative positions taken in marks at the beginning of this week were predominantly short-term plays and have nearly all be unwound again.
EU leaders convene for a summit in Amsterdam on Monday, where the final review of the Maastricht Treaty on EMU and post-EMU budgetary stability pact are expected to be agreed.

Last-minute jitters about the success of the summit and the timetable for the single currency have been raised since the newly-elected Socialist government in France has insisted on the inclusion of a more pro-employment bias to the stability pact.

These reservations triggered concerns about a delay to the 1999 EMU start and saw speculative knee-jerk buying of marks on Monday. Official comments through the week, however, convinced traders the project will start on time whatever the compromise.
"This was such a confusing week in terms of gauging sentiment that the only safe place to park your money is in the dollar or sterling," said a trader at a UK fund managment firm.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl and his Finance Minister Theo Waigel met French President Jacques Chirac, his prime minister Lional Jospin and French finance minister Dominque Strauss-Kahn.
Their raft of comments all pointed to progress on an agreement at or before Monday's EU summit but that further work was needed. All said they wanted EMU on time in 1999.
EU finance ministers hold a pre-summit meeting on Sunday night to find a common solution to the new French demands.

The market preference for non-EMU currencies while EU politicians sort out their differences has also seen sterling dragged up against the beleagured mark. The pound rose to its highest level since August 1992 at 2.8420 in late trade Friday.
In the U.S., meantime, the unexpected 0.3 percent drop in the May PPI initially dented the dollar as speculation about a rise in U.S. interest rates on July 1-2 waned.
However, the storming performannce of U.S. stocks and the drain of funds out of the mark and continental Europe quickly offset any negative effects on the currency.
"I think the May PPI precludes any chance of a Fed tightening in July," said Hawkins at Bank of America.
The University of Michigan's preliminary consumer confidence index for June later showed an expected rise to 103.4 from 103.2 in May.

The dollar was firmer against the yen too, testing resistance about 115 yen in late trade. Traders said the focus there would now be the Group of Seven industrialised nations summit at the end of the next week. Extreme volatility in the pairing would ebb further until that moves out of the way.
--Mike Dolan, London newsroom +44 171 652 6762
